title: Special coordinate determined by the statistic
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, let $z$ be an achievable value of the statistic recording the transcript, the special coordinate, Alice’s bits before it, and Bob’s bits after it, and let $\omega$ be a hard sample. If the statistic of $\omega$ under $p$ equals $z$, then the special coordinate of $\omega$ equals the special-coordinate component of $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol on length-$n$ disjointness inputs
replaced:
Fix a disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$, and recall that the special
coordinate of a hard-distribution sample $\omega$ is the index $T$ selected by that
sample. Let $z$ be an achievable value of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$,
whose special-coordinate component records the index $T$. If the $Z$ value produced by
$\omega$ under $p$ equals $z$, then the special coordinate of $\omega$ coincides with
the special-coordinate component of $z$.
